answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, so votes from a sybil island depend on paths entering it, not merely on its internal attestations. For a cluster S, conductance φ(S)=cut(S,¬S)/vol(S) measures its sparse external ledge: under stationary sampling, low conductance limits the probability a walk crosses into S. With bounded walk length and capped per-node influence, that leakage bounds aggregate voting weight; a gale of internal attestations cannot manufacture external trust.
